title: A finitely presented sheaf flat at a point has projective affine sections after an elementary etale base neighbourhood
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and suppose that $\mathcal G_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. There exist an affine scheme $S^{\prime}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], an etale morphism $e:S^{\prime}\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $s^{\prime}\in S^{\prime}$ with $e(s^{\prime})=s$ inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s^{\prime})$ [def-weil-residue-field], and an affine open [def-weil-open-immersion] $W\subseteq X\times_S S^{\prime}$ [def-pc-fibre-product] containing the unique point over $(x,s^{\prime})$, such that $\Gamma(W,(\operatorname{pr}_X^*\mathcal G)|_W)$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is a projective $\Gamma(S^{\prime},\mathcal O_{S^{\prime}})$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. No finite-generation hypothesis over this base ring is imposed.

proof.text: Choose affine neighbourhoods $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $s$ and $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset f^{-1}(S_0)$ of $x$ on which $G=\mathcal G|_{X_0}$ has a finite presentation, as allowed by the hypotheses. The all-affine-pairs theorem gives $A\to B$ finitely presented. The affine dictionary writes $G=\widetilde M$ with $M$ finitely presented over $B$; its stalk at a prime $\mathfrak q$ is $M_{\mathfrak q}$. At $x$, with base prime $\mathfrak p$, the assumed $A_{\mathfrak p}$-flatness implies $A$-flatness by flatness of localization and transitivity. Apply algebraic openness of flatness to $(A,B,M)$ to get an open neighbourhood of $x$ where every $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat. Such a module is flat over $A_{\mathfrak q\cap A}$: for an injection of $A_{\mathfrak q\cap A}$-modules, its tensor with $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is the same as its tensor over $A$, since every inverted scalar already acts invertibly. Choose a smaller affine $X_0$ inside this open. The stalk criterion says $G$ is flat over $S_0$. Restriction preserves the displayed finite presentations and quasi-coherence.

The affine fibre $(X_0)_s$ is the spectrum of a finite type $\kappa(s)$-algebra, hence has Noetherian coordinate ring: a field has only the ideals zero and one, and finite type algebras over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian. Pullback of the local finite presentation of $G$ gives a finite presentation of $G_s$. The affine dictionary and finiteness of associated primes of a finite module over a Noetherian ring show that $E=\operatorname{Ass}_{(X_0)_s}(G_s)$ is finite. For every $a\in E$ which does not specialize to $x$, remove the closed subset $\overline{\{a\}}$ of $X_0$. None contains $x$, and removing their finite union leaves an open neighbourhood of $x$. Choose a smaller affine $X_0$ therein. On an open subscheme the stalks and their annihilators are unchanged; thus every remaining associated point of $G_s$ specializes to $x$. Finite presentation over $S_0$ still holds by the affine-pairs theorem and the qcqs permanence lemma. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S_0$ was used.

source.place: Tag 05ME, first paragraph, shrinking the special-fibre assassin; divisors.tex Tags 02OK and 05AF.

proof.text: Apply the pointwise projective-chart theorem to $X_0/S_0$, $G$, and $x$. Write its affine elementary base neighbourhood as $(S_1,s_1)\to(S_0,s)$ and its affine source neighbourhood as $g:(Y,y)\to(X_0,x)$, with $q:Y\to S_1$. Put $X_1=X_0\times_{S_0}S_1$. The induced map $h=(g,q):Y\to X_1$ is etale: $X_1\to X_0$ is etale by base change, and its composite with $h$ is the etale $g$, so etale cancellation applies. Its marked point maps to the unique $x_1$ above $(x,s_1)$. Moreover $Y\to S_1$ is finitely presented: $Y\to X_0\to S_0$ is locally finitely presented by composition, $S_1\to S_0$ is locally of finite type, and finite-presentation cancellation makes $q$ locally finitely presented; $Y,S_1$ affine then give qcqs. Put $F=\operatorname{pr}_{X_0}^*G$ and $H=h^*F\cong g^*G$. The chart theorem gives $Q=\Gamma(Y,H)$ projective over $A_1=\Gamma(S_1,\mathcal O)$. Both sheaves remain quasi-coherent and finitely presented, and $F$ remains flat over $S_1$. The specified residue isomorphism identifies the fibre $(X_1)_{s_1}$, its sheaf and its marked point with $(X_0)_s,G_s,x$. Thus all its associated points specialize to $x_1$; this persists under every further elementary pointed base neighbourhood.

source.place: Tag 05ME, first paragraph, projective etale chart; Tag 05ID supplies a pointwise chart instead of the unused whole-fibre covering of Tag 05KW.

proof.text: Projectivity of $Q$ makes it $A_1$-flat. The affine-chart flatness criterion then makes $H$ flat over $S_1$. Apply the affine projectivity-purity theorem to $Y/S_1$ and $H$: its hypotheses are finite presentation of the morphism and sheaf, quasi-coherence, and the flatness just checked. It follows that $H$ is universally pure over $S_1$. Since $h$ is etale, its image is open. Choose an affine open $U\subseteq h(Y)$ containing $x_1$. We will show $F|_U$ is pure along $U_{s_1}$.

source.place: Tag 05ME, end of first paragraph and beginning of second paragraph; Tags 05K6 and 05MD.

proof.text: Test purity using its definition. Take an arbitrary elementary etale neighbourhood $(T,t)\to(S_1,s_1)$, a specialization $t'\leadsto t$, and $\xi\in\operatorname{Ass}_{U_T/T}(F_T|_{U_T})$ over $t'$. Put $Y_T=Y\times_{S_1}T$, and let $h_T:Y_T\to(X_1)_T$ be the base-changed etale map. The restriction $h^{-1}(U)\to U$ is etale and surjective by the definition of its image; its arbitrary base change to $U_T$ remains surjective by the etale-covering base-change theorem. Choose $\xi'\in Y_T$ above $\xi$. On the $t'$ fibres the schemes are locally Noetherian, being locally of finite type over the field $\kappa(t')$. Etale invariance of associated points applied to $(h_T)_{t'}$ implies $\xi'\in\operatorname{Ass}_{Y_T/T}(H_T)$. Here association on the open $U_T$ agrees with association in $(X_1)_T$ by the identical local stalks. Universal purity of $H$, with this arbitrary $T\to S_1$, supplies a specialization of $\xi'$ to some point of $(Y_T)_t$.

source.place: Tag 05ME, last paragraph: lifting a relative associated point to the etale chart and using its universal purity.

proof.text: We need the limiting point to be associated. Form $Z=\overline{\{\xi'\}}\subset Y_T$ with its reduced induced closed-scheme structure. Its fibre $Z_t$ is nonempty by step 5. Choose an irreducible component $C$ of $Z_t$ and its generic point $y$, using component coverage and sobriety of schemes. Thus $\xi'\leadsto y$. The module $H_T$ is flat over $T$ by base change of $H$; it is also quasi-coherent and finitely presented, and $Y_T/T$ is finitely presented, by base change of the data in step 4. Apply the existing relative-associated-specialization theorem (Tag 0GSI) to $Y_T/T$, $H_T$, $\xi'$, and this component $C$. In particular its required flatness at $y$ holds. Its conclusion gives $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_{(Y_T)_t}((H_T)_t)$. The dimension clause of that theorem is not needed.

source.place: Tag 05ME, last paragraph, application of Tag 05L3; its associated-specialization input is more-morphisms.tex Tag 0GSI.

proof.text: The map $(h_T)_t:(Y_T)_t\to((X_1)_T)_t$ is etale between locally Noetherian schemes over $\kappa(t)$. Etale assassin invariance sends the associated point $y$ of step 6 to an associated point $h_T(y)$ of $((F_T)_t)$. Since $\kappa(t)=\kappa(s_1)$ through the specified elementary-neighbourhood isomorphism, the fibre identification in step 3 says that $h_T(y)$ specializes to the point $x_t$ above $x_1$. This point lies in $U_T$. Opens contain all generalizations of their points: if an open containing $x_t$ omitted $h_T(y)$, its closed complement would contain its specialization $x_t$. Therefore $h_T(y)\in(U_T)_t$. Continuity sends $\xi'\leadsto y$ to $\xi\leadsto h_T(y)$. We have found a specialization in $(U_T)_t$ for every proposed impurity in step 5. By definition, $F|_U$ is pure along $U_{s_1}$.

source.place: Tag 05ME, final sentences: g(x\prime) is associated, specializes to x, and hence belongs to U.

proof.text: The map $U\to S_1$ is finitely presented: $X_1/S_1$ is locally of finite presentation by base change, restriction to $U$ preserves this local property by composition with the etale open inclusion, and a locally finitely presented map from an affine scheme to the affine $S_1$ is finitely presented by qcqs permanence. The module $F|_U$ is quasi-coherent, finitely presented and flat over $S_1$. By openness of purity, the set of $v\in S_1$ for which $F|_U$ is pure along $U_v$ is an open neighbourhood of $s_1$. Choose an affine open $V$ inside it containing $s_1$, and put $W=U\times_{S_1}V$. Since $U\to S_1$ is a map of affine schemes, it is affine, so $W$ is affine. It is an open subscheme of $X_0\times_{S_0}V$, contains the unique point above $(x,s_1)$, and its module is pure relative to $V$: every elementary neighbourhood of a point in the open $V$ is also one in $S_1$, with the same relevant fibre and specializations. Finite presentation of $W/V$ and relative flatness of its module survive base change.

source.place: Tag 05ME, second paragraph: shrink S using lemma-flat-finite-presentation-purity-open.

proof.text: Apply the affine projectivity-purity equivalence to $W/V$: both schemes are affine, the map and module are finitely presented, and the module is relatively flat and pure relative to $V$, by step 8. It gives $\Gamma(W,F_W)$ projective over $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. Finally the composite $V\to S_1\to S_0\to S$ is etale: open immersions are etale and etale maps compose. It sends the retained point to $s$ with unchanged residue field. The open $W\subseteq X_0\times_{S_0}V$ is also open in $X\times_SV$, since $X_0\subset f^{-1}(S_0)$ was an open subscheme. Pullback composition identifies $F_W$ with $(\operatorname{pr}_X^*\mathcal G)|_W$. Taking $S'=V$ proves every requested clause, with arbitrary-rank projectivity rather than finite projectivity.

source.place: Tag 05ME, second paragraph: proposition-finite-presentation-flat-pure-is-projective and the initial permitted replacements.
